page: The Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g-960s is a balanced general-purpose virtual instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute series. Powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor family, the instance allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores at a baseline clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions. System memory provides 64 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration via dedicated GPUs is not included, but the instance comes bundled with 960 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark measurements demonstrate strong single-thread efficiency alongside reliable multi-core throughput. In synthetic tests, the instance records top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng tests (3,622.78), gzip compression (39.34 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (17.66 GB/sec). Geekbench text processing also achieves top-tier results at 3,039.0 points. While single-thread efficiency and memory scores (2,803.28 in PassMark) sit in upper percentiles, broader multi-core benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core (11,775.0) and multi-threaded decompression (137.08 GB/sec), remain in the average tier. Small-scale language model inference exhibits rapid text generation (443.84 tokens/sec on 135M models), though throughput moderates to standard performance profiles on 7B parameter models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the vx1-g-16c-64g-960s provides high resource density by pairing dedicated compute cores with substantial high-speed NVMe storage on a single instance. This local integration avoids the latency and recurring expenses associated with separate network-attached block volumes. Given its 1:4 memory allocation, high single-threaded responsiveness, and local disk capacity, this server profile is technically configured for production databases, Redis caches, static and dynamic web application hosting, build systems, and general backend services requiring sustained I/O throughput.

Memory bandwidth and PassMark memory metrics reflect strong memory subsystem efficiency. The instance accommodates enterprise web serving, relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, build pipelines, and general enterprise backend workloads.
